text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. To access protected resources, you often need authentication, such as an API key or token. Be careful with rate limits, because sending too many requests can get you blocked. Finally, always add error handling to your code. This way, your application can respond properly when something goes wrong, such as a bad request or a server failure.
